lede: The biggest thing to track this week is Tuesday's CommonSpirit Health presentation to the Telluride Hospital District board — no packet is public yet, but with a Letter of Intent already in motion, this is the kind of closed-door conversation that shapes how this valley gets medical care for decades. Alongside that, the Housing Authority Subcommittee takes up the thorny question of subpar bedrooms in mitigation units, and the county's housing code working group meets for its eighth session on stripping Land Use Code barriers to workforce housing. HARC also has an unusual one: a work session on potentially demolishing Rebekah Hall, the town-owned building where the commission itself meets.

notable.stake: CommonSpirit partnership terms could shape local hospital care for generations.
Policy decisions on subpar bedrooms directly affect workforce housing unit compliance.
County housing code rewrite could remove key barriers to affordable housing production.
Potential demolition of town-owned Rebekah Hall is on the table for review.
BOCC takes up a view-plain MOU and two constitutional amendment discussions.
Two public hearings on a PUD application and a parcel subdivision in Ouray County.
